rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God retains the soul whose death is decreed, while the soul taken in sleep returns to its body upon waking until its appointed death.
rows.anchor: المقصود من الآية أنه تعالى يتوفى الأنفس عند الموت وعند النوم إلا أنه يمسك الأنفس التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human soul is a luminous spiritual substance: waking illuminates the whole body, sleep withdraws its light partly from the exterior, and death withdraws it entirely.
rows.anchor: النفس الإنسانية عبارة عن جوهر مشرق روحاني إذا تعلق بالبدن حصل ضوؤه في جميع الأعضاء وهو الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different, carefully ordered relations between soul and body at waking, sleep, and death demonstrate a powerful, knowing, wise Creator; they also call people to worship God rather than inert idols.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا التدبير العجيب لا يمكن صدوره إلا عن القادر العليم الحكيم

words: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists said they worshipped idols as images of God’s favored servants so those figures would intercede for them.
rows.anchor: نحن لا نعبد هذه الأصنام لاعتقاد أنها آلهة تضر وتنفع وإنما نعبدها لأجل أنها تماثيل لأشخاص كانوا عند الله من المقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither lifeless idols nor the honored people depicted by them can independently intercede; only God grants intercession, so worship is due to Him, who owns heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: الأصنام لا تملك شيئا ولا تعقل شيئا فكيف يعقل صدور الشفاعة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not deny intercession absolutely; it teaches that no one can intercede unless God gives permission.
rows.anchor: نسلم أنه سبحانه ما لم يأذن في الشفاعة لم يقدر أحد على الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true agent of taking souls, while He delegates this work among created causes to the Angel of Death as chief and other angels as assistants.
rows.anchor: المتوفى في الحقيقة هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance remains obligatory and fear of punishment remains because sinners cannot know punishment is wholly removed: God may forgive outright or forgive after a period in Hell.
rows.anchor: عندنا التوبة واجبة وخوف العقاب قائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling sinners servants evokes their need, humility, and poverty, qualities that invite a generous Lord to give mercy.
rows.anchor: المذنب بالعبد والعبودية مفسرة بالحاجة والذلة والمسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s possessive attribution of the sinners to Himself honors them and reassures them against punishment.
rows.anchor: أضافهم إلى نفسه بياء الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damage of sins returns to the sinners themselves, so they need no additional harm imposed on them.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن ضرر تلك الذنوب ما عاد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidding despair commands hope, and a generous Lord’s command to hope is a promise of generosity.
rows.anchor: نهاهم عن القنوط فيكون هذا أمرا بالرجاء والكريم إذا أمر بالرجاء فلا يليق به إلا الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says “God’s mercy” rather than “My mercy,” invoking God’s greatest name and therefore the greatest kind of mercy and favor.
rows.anchor: لأن قولنا الله أعظم أسماء الله وأجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating God’s name and adding the emphatic particle إن intensifies the promise of mercy.
rows.anchor: بل أعاد اسم الله وقرن به لفظة إن المفيدة لأعظم وجوه التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “all” reinforces the comprehensive promise of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فقال جميعا وهذا أيضا من المؤكدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Forgiving” signals removal of grounds for punishment, while “the Merciful” signals the granting of grounds for mercy and reward.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى تحصيل موجبات الرحمة والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic pronoun yields exclusivity: only God is truly forgiving and merciful, displaying perfection in both attributes.
rows.anchor: أنه لا غفور ولا رحيم إلا هو

rows.speaker: أهل مكة
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that Meccans, having worshipped idols and killed people, wondered how they could accept Islam if Muhammad said such sins would not be forgiven.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها نزلت في أهل مكة فإنهم قالوا يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس لم يغفر له

rows.speaker: وحشي قاتل حمزة
rows.claim: Another report says Wahshi, Hamza’s killer, feared his repentance would not be accepted when he wanted to convert; after the verse he embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة لما أراد أن يسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked whether the promise to Wahshi was exclusive or for Muslims generally, the Prophet replied that it applied generally.
rows.anchor: فقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه له خاصة أم للمسلمين عامة

rows.speaker: أناس أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية
rows.claim: A further reported occasion is people who committed grave sins in pre-Islamic times and feared Islam would not bring acceptance of their repentance.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أناس أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد
rows.claim: The verse was also said to concern Ayyash, al-Walid, and other Muslims who apostatized under persecution; Umar sent them the verses, after which they returned to Islam and emigrated.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين أسلموا ثم فتنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reports give particular occasions, the general wording governs and the verse is not restricted to those cases.
rows.anchor: العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب فنزول هذه الآيات في هذه الوقائع لا يمنع من عمومها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim read the final ya of “عبادي” with fatḥ; the other readers, and some Asim transmissions, do not.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers retain the ya in pausal form except Abu Bakr’s transmission from Asim, which pauses without it.
rows.anchor: كلهم يقفون عليه بإثبات الياء لأنها ثابتة في المصحف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Abu Amr and al-Kisai read the nun in “taqnaṭū” with kasra; the others read it with fatḥa, and both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي تقنطوا بكسر النون والباقون بفتحها وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud adds “for whom He wills” after the promise to forgive all sins.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عباس ، وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses turning back as repentance, submission, and sincere action; he says it follows the forgiveness promise to show repentance is a necessary condition.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) أي وتوبوا إليه وأسلموا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls al-Zamakhshari’s explanation very weak: repentance is obligatory, while forgiveness may occur directly or after punishment, and repentance removes that punishment.
rows.anchor: وأقول هذا الكلام ضعيف جدا لأن عندنا التوبة عن المعاصي واجبة فلم يلزم من ورود الأمر بها طعن في الوعد بالمغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of “the best of what was sent down” is the Qur’an, supported by the description “best discourse.”
rows.anchor: أنه القرآن ومعناه واتبعوا القرآن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as obeying God and avoiding disobedience: revealed material includes what is bad to avoid, lesser things not to desire, and the best to follow.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن معناه ، والتزموا طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation identifies the best revelation as the abrogating ruling rather than the abrogated one, citing God’s promise of a better or equivalent replacement.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأحسن الناسخ دون المنسوخ

words: مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ بَغْتَةً
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden punishment warning threatens and frightens people by describing punishment that overtakes them while they are unaware.
rows.anchor: والمراد منه التهديد والتخويف والمعنى أنه يفجأ العذاب وأنتم غافلون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That a soul should say” is in the accusative as a purpose expression, meaning lest or for fear that it should say this.
rows.anchor: مفعول له أي كراهة أن تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “a soul” may denote a particular soul distinguished by especially persistent sin.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تراد نفس ممتازة عن سائر النفوس لأجل اختصاصها بمزيد إضرار بما لا ينفي رغبتها في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite noun can be general: because regret naturally follows neglect of obedience, the construction implies that such regret occurs for every such neglect.
rows.anchor: علم أصول الفقه أن الحكم المذكور عقيب وصف يناسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who affirm divine bodily parts cite “God’s side,” but Razi rejects bodily meaning because arguments against divine parts require interpretation.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن دلائلنا على نفي الأعضاء قد كثرت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains neglecting God’s side as forfeiting God’s reward.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد ضيعت من ثواب الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mقاتل explains it as neglecting remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل ضيعت من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains it as neglecting God’s command.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد في أمر الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains it as neglecting obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains it as neglecting God’s due.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير في حق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi derives “side” from a thing’s aspect or component and extends it by analogy to what belongs to or follows from a thing, such as God’s cause, command, or obedience; a poetic line supports the usage.
rows.anchor: الجنب سمي جنبا لأنه جانب من جوانب ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports “ya hasratī” as the original form and “ya hasratāy” as combining the substitute with what it replaces.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) قرىء { * يا حسرتي } على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner says he not only neglected obedience but also mocked religion and its adherents.
rows.anchor: أي أنه ما كان مكتفيا بذلك التقصير بل كان من المستهزئين بالدين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the sinner was not content with neglecting obedience but mocked those who practiced it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى سخر من أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “though I was among the mockers” is accusative as a circumstantial clause: he neglected God’s cause while mocking.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحالة كأنه قال : فرطت في جنب الله وأنا ساخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned person voices three responses: regret at neglected obedience, an excuse that God did not guide him, and a wish to return and act well.
rows.anchor: أتى بثلاثة أشياء أولها : الحسرة على التفريط في الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the excuse of lacking guidance: signs had already come, but the sinner denied them, acted arrogantly, and disbelieved.
rows.anchor: لأن الهداية كانت حاصرة والأعذار زائلة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “balā” answers an implied negation: “if God had guided me” means that He had not guided me, so “balā” appropriately denies that premise.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج بلى جواب النفي وليس في الكلام لفظ النفي

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the well-known reading addresses the soul in masculine because “soul” can denote either a man or a woman.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : القراءة المشهورة واقعة على التذكير

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس عن أم سلمة
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas relates from Umm Salama that the Prophet read the clause in feminine form; Abu Ubayd says it would be authoritative if sound but is not musnad because al-Rabi did not meet her.
rows.anchor: وروى الربيع بن أنس عن أم سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine agreement is grammatically apt because “soul” is feminine in the Qur’an in most usages, as in the examples cited.
rows.anchor: لفظ النفس ورد في القرآن في أكثر الأمر على التأنيث

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues human acts are theirs because blame for excess, requests for forgiveness, and commands to repent and follow revelation presuppose agency and ability before punishment.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي هذه الآيات دالة على صحة القول بالقدر من وجوه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi adds that regret for neglected obedience, reproach for mockery, and the sinner’s claim that guidance would have enabled piety all presuppose that these acts were within human power.
rows.anchor: ولا يتحسر المرء على أمر سبق منه إلا وكان يصح منه أن يفعله

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the wishes for guidance, piety, another return, and good deeds make no sense if God gave the person only an unchangeable capacity for unbelief.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي هذه الآيات دالة على صحة القول بالقدر

words: بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ ءَايَٰتِى فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that God’s reproach for denying signs, arrogance, and disbelief treats them as chosen acts; otherwise people could blame God for creating their denial and withholding belief.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى أن الحجة عليهم لله لأن الحجة لهم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that Qur’anic passages also attribute misguidance, restraint, gentleness, hardening, and gradual entrapment to God; his commentary has already treated these counterarguments extensively.
rows.anchor: القرآن مملوء من أن الله تعالى يضل ويمنع ويصدر منه اللين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because resurrection is certain and only obedience benefits people then, obedience is urgent; supplication and humble pleading are the noblest kinds, so God commands them here.
rows.anchor: وكان من المعلوم بالضرورة أن الإنسان لا ينتفع في يوم القيامة إلا بطاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read “call upon Me” as prayer, others as worship because the next clause says “My worship” and Qur’anic usage can equate calling with worship.
rows.anchor: واختلف الناس في المراد بقوله { ادعوني }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against construing “call” as worship, Razi says supplication itself confesses servitude, need, and lowliness; abandoning it can reflect pride about displaying servitude.
rows.anchor: الدعاء هو اعتراف بالعبودية والذلة والمسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply to the worship reading is that one should not leave the apparent meaning unless there is separate evidence requiring that shift.
rows.anchor: بأن ترك الظاهرة لا يصار إليه إلا بدليل منفصل

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaabi says the promise applies when the requested outcome is beneficial and wise; he then asks what prayer adds if God already does what is best.
rows.anchor: أجاب الكعبي عنه بأن قال : الدعاء إنما يصح على شرط

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaabi replies that prayer draws a person into reliance on God, and that the same determinist objection applies whether an act is known to occur or not to occur.
rows.anchor: أجاب الكعبي عنه بأن قال : الدعاء إنما يصح على شرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says a prayer is genuine only when the heart has no reliance on wealth, status, relatives, friends, or personal effort; tongue-only prayer relies on other means, while a heart wholly turned to God is answered.
rows.anchor: فكل من دعا الله وفي قلبه ذرة من الاعتماد على ماله وجاهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account gives glad tidings: complete detachment from everything besides God comes near death, when a person knows nothing can help but divine favor, so prayer then should be accepted.
rows.anchor: أن انقطاع القلب بالكلية عما سوى الله لا يحصل إلا عند القرب من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi notes that his fuller discussion of supplication appeared earlier in Surat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الكلام السمتقصى في الدعاء قد سبق ذكره في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Dākhirīn” means humbled and abased.
rows.anchor: أي صاغرين وهذا إحسان عظيم من الله تعالى حيث ذكر الوعيد الشديد على ترك الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe threat for abandoning supplication is itself a great kindness from God.
rows.anchor: وهذا إحسان عظيم من الله تعالى حيث ذكر الوعيد الشديد على ترك الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command connects to prior blessings: since God granted great favors before people asked, He can grant lesser requests after they ask.
rows.anchor: إني أنعمت عليك قبل طلبك لهذه النعم الجليلة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command also follows proof of knowledge: supplication presupposes recognizing God, so the preceding passage supplies ten signs of His existence, power, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: الاشتغال بالدعاء لا بد وأن يكون مسبوقا بحصول المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Humble” means subdued and diminished; the word is metaphorically applied to earth when it lacks rain and vegetation.
rows.anchor: والخشوع التذلل والتصاغر ، واستعير هذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth stirs with new growth and swells as plants approach emergence, lifting and splitting the soil.
rows.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات ، وربت : انتفخت لأن النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who revives dead earth can revive dead bodies; the earth’s renewal is evidence for bodily resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني أن القادر على إحياء الأرض بعد موتها هو القادر على إحياء هذه الأجساد بعد موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reassembling scattered bodily parts is possible, as is restoring life, intellect, and ability to them; since God can do all possibilities, bodily resurrection is plainly possible.
rows.anchor: عودة التأليف والتركيب إلى تلك الأجزاء المتفرقة ممكن لذاته
